also: just the person I was looking for
the very person I was looking for

evidence: Ter. And. 125–126: attat! hoc illud est
terms.comment: Lewis & Short (s.v. atat, also spelt attat, attatae): joy, pain, wonder, fright, warning. Of a dismayed discovery it is “uh-oh” (see oh no!).

evidence: Plaut. Poen. 768: Hahahae, jam teneō quid sit, perspexī modo.
terms.comment: Lewis & Short (s.v. ha): laughter or derision; here the laugh of a man who has seen through something.

evidence: Plaut. Mil. 36b: Ehem, sciō jam quid vīs dīcere.

phrases.latin: attat! hoc illud est: hinc illae lacrumae
phrases.english: Aha! so that’s it: hence those tears

phrases.latin: attat, sciō cūr tē patrem adsimulēs esse et mē fīlium
phrases.english: aha, I know why you pretend to be my father and me your son

phrases.latin: Hahahae, jam teneō quid sit, perspexī modo.
phrases.english: Aha, now I get it; I’ve just seen through it.

phrases.latin: Ehem, sciō jam quid vīs dīcere.
phrases.english: Ah, now I know what you mean.
Aha, the very person I was looking for!

sources: Lewis & Short: atat · Lewis & Short: ha (hahahae) · Lewis & Short: ehem
